rule: Each case names its input, the required and forbidden outcomes, the contracts (T..) and capability rows (CR..) it exercises, the existing evidence that already pins part of it, and the node whose test makes it executable. The stub cases (PC03-PC06) are type-level proofs CPF1 compiles in crates/verter_compiler/tests/cases/carrier_frontend_backend_split_proof.rs; the stubs are test-only types, never production registrations. Work counters (WC..) are reported by CPF1 as counts and growth ratios against the baseline commit, measured on the same worker in the same session; timing, allocation and memory figures are evidence only and never gate.

cases.name: Vue keeps every product through the split
cases.input: The pinned Vue corpus through parse, registered geometry, eval source, template facts, IDE projection and a client+server runtime compile
cases.required: Authored bytes, parse facts, recovery, diagnostics, registered geometry, IDE companion bytes and maps, runtime bytes and maps, template facts and cache hits are byte-equal to the baseline commit; one frontend parse per parse key
cases.forbidden: Any output, map or diagnostic divergence; a second parse of one parse key; a frontend module whose closure reaches an LC module

cases.name: Svelte keeps every product through the split
cases.input: The pinned Svelte corpus, runes and legacy files, through parse, registered geometry, template facts, IDE projection and a client+server runtime compile
cases.required: As PC01, including the official parse-defect codes and their encounter order
cases.forbidden: As PC01; a parse-defect code that changes because its selection moved out of the runtime module

cases.name: Tooling-only HTML frontend stub
cases.input: A test-only HtmlCarrierFrontend implementing CarrierFrontend only, registered as a frontend row with no semantic, projection or compiler-backend row
cases.required: The registration compiles and the frontend registry accepts it; parse, registered geometry and parse diagnostics are served; the compiler-backend registry has no row for it
cases.forbidden: A RuntimeCompilerBackend, FrameworkHostIntegrationBackend or CarrierCompilerBackend implementation for the stub, including one that returns Unsupported; a runtime accessor on its row (compile error)

cases.name: Tooling-only Astro frontend and projection stub
cases.input: A test-only AstroCarrierFrontend plus AstroProjectionBackend, registered with a frontend row and a projection row and no compiler-backend row
cases.required: The registrations compile; an IDE-companion demand is admitted and served through the projection row with no compiler-backend row present
cases.forbidden: An IDE demand that requires, consults or refuses because of a missing compiler backend; an Unsupported compiler implementation

cases.name: Frontend closure is free of runtime codegen
cases.input: The Vue, Svelte, HTML-stub and Astro-stub frontend modules
cases.required: Each frontend module compiles with no path to compile, compile_transaction, assembly, standalone, svelte::runtime, style_planner, template::code_gen, script codegen or tsc, proven by visibility or module/crate structure
cases.forbidden: A frontend that reaches an LC module directly or through a carrier-compiler struct; a name-keyed source scanner standing in for the structural proof
existingEvidence: verter_compiler tests/cases/compiler_layer_dependency_closure.rs (crate-level closure only; it states it does not prove an in-crate split)

cases.name: Compile demand on a carrier without a backend
cases.input: A runtime compile demand on the HTML stub; then a mixed demand (IDE companion plus runtime) on the Astro stub
cases.required: The runtime product reports capability status UNSUPPORTED; the Astro IDE companion is still produced; no other product changes
cases.forbidden: An error diagnostic or failed request on a tooling path; a fallback to another carrier's backend; a partial result promoted warm

cases.name: Template facts without a compiler
cases.input: Vue and Svelte files whose template facts are demanded with no compile demand
cases.required: Facts and template-expression diagnostics equal the baseline; no runtime compile entry, compile target or code generator runs
cases.forbidden: Facts computed through compile_from_parsed_legacy or any CompileTarget; facts that lose their expression diagnostics

cases.name: One registration authority
cases.input: Duplicate frontend rows for one carrier profile; a compiler-backend row whose carrier has no frontend row
cases.required: Both registrations fail construction with a typed duplicate or missing-frontend error
cases.forbidden: A combined registry or carrier-compiler struct alive beside the two registries; first-registered-wins

workCounters.source: CPF1 counts registered frontend parse entries at InstalledCarrierFrontend::parse and exposes the reader as pub under cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support")), the same exposure as take_projection_producer_invocations, so crates/verter_compiler/tests/cases/carrier_frontend_backend_split_proof.rs can read it. registered_frontend_parse_count is #[cfg(test)] pub(super) and is not this source. verter_audit CarrierParse (compiler.carrier_parse) records parse bytes at compile::parse_sfc and the Svelte tokenizer, not the parse-entry count. Excluded: StandaloneCompiler::compile and prepare (standalone.rs compile_vue, compile_svelte and prepare_unrecorded) never enter InstalledCarrierFrontend::parse. Those parses are F-C13. This ratio is the registered frontend entry on PC01 and PC02 only. CPF1's cutover makes the direct route consume the admitted frontend parse, the way lower_vue_from_parsed and lower_svelte_from_parsed already do, instead of calling parse_sfc or parse_svelte. This counter is not widened and no second counter is added
catalog lookups per demand (frontend, semantic, projection, backend), counted by CPF1 at the registry entry
workCounters.baselineRelation: reported with the growth ratio against the baseline's catalog and enum dispatches; no hidden second lookup per product
equal; zero runtime compile entries on a facts-only demand

workCounters.source: runtime compile and host-admission executions per demand
workCounters.baselineRelation: equal for Vue/Svelte compile demands; zero for every tooling-only demand

workCounters.source: verter_audit attribution SourceTextCopy, CodeTransformRender and SourceMapBuild counts
workCounters.baselineRelation: reported with growth ratios; no new copy of source text or parse artifact per product
